questions.text:
enum E { A = 1 }
E.A = 9
console.log(E.A)
console.log(E[1])
console.log(E[9])

enum E { A = 0, B = 0 }
console.log(E[0])

const s = "b"
enum E { A = s }
console.log(E.A)
console.log(E["b"])

enum E { A = -1, B }
console.log(E.B)

enum E { A = "a", B = A }
console.log(E.B)

type T = `id-${number}`
const s: T = "id-4"
console.log(s)

type T = 1 extends number ? 2 : 3
const n: T = 2
console.log(n)

const o = { n: 1, m: 2 } as { n: number }
console.log(o.m)

function f<T = number>(x: T) { return x }
console.log(typeof f("a"))

const t = [1] as const
;(t as unknown as number[]).push(2)
console.log(t.length)

class A { constructor(public n = 3) {} }
console.log(new A().n)

class A { constructor(public n?: number) {} }
console.log(new A().n)

const x: { t: "a"; n: number } | { t: "b"; s: string } = { t: "a", n: 5 }
console.log(x.n)

const s = Symbol("a") as unique symbol
console.log(typeof s)

const f: () => void = () => 1
console.log(f())

class A { declare n: number }
console.log(Object.hasOwn(new A(), "n"))
What does merging two enum blocks with the same name produce?
options: One enum object with the members of both blocks
Two objects, and the second shadows the first
A compile error in every case

questions.text: What does merging two namespace blocks produce?
options: One object with the exports of both blocks

questions.text: What does declare do to a value?
options: It creates a variable set to undefined
It tells the checker the binding exists and emits no JS for it
It turns the value into the type never

questions.text: When do subclass field initializers run relative to the base constructor?
options: Only on the first read of the field

questions.text: In which order do stacked class decorators run?
What can a class decorator return?
options: A replacement constructor. The original class is the argument

questions.text: What can a method decorator return?
options: A function that replaces that method
Nothing. The return value is ignored

questions.text: When does using call Symbol.dispose?
options: Only if you call dispose yourself

questions.text: In which order are two using bindings in one block disposed?
What does using null do?
options: Nothing. null is allowed and has nothing to call

questions.text: What happens to a numeric enum reverse mapping if you assign a new value to the member?
options: The old entry is removed and a new one is created
The enum object is frozen and the write throws
The old reverse entry stays. A new one is not created
The reverse mapping is rebuilt from scratch

questions.text: If two numeric members share a value, which name does the reverse mapping keep?
options: Neither. The reverse entry becomes undefined

questions.text: Does a string enum member computed from a variable get a reverse mapping?
options: Yes, from the string back to the name
Yes, but only when the string is one character

questions.text: What does merging an interface into a class add at runtime?
options: An own property set to undefined

questions.text: Where does a class method live compared with a class field that holds a function?
options: The method is on the prototype. The field is an own property of the instance
The method is on the instance and the field is on the prototype

questions.text: What is a phantom brand number & { __brand: "m" } at runtime?
options: An instance of a Brand class
Still a number. The brand is erased

questions.text: From where can a # field be read?
options: Only from the class body that declared it, including on a subclass instance
Through a string key from outside
Only from a static block, not from a method

questions.text: What does a conditional type A extends B ? C : D become in JS?
options: A function that picks a branch at the call
Nothing. JS only contains a value you actually wrote
An object { true: C, false: D }

questions.text: What does a mapped type emit by itself?
options: A class with a getter per key
Nothing. The object you build stays a plain object

questions.text: What does a default type parameter T = number do to a string argument?
options: It converts the string to number
It throws because the default is number
It wraps the string in a Number object
Nothing to the value. The default applies only when the type argument is omitted, and it is erased
